phase2Candidates.name: custom single-choice select interaction
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Both consumers copy the same native-select ownership, keyboard, focus, dynamic-sync, width-policy, and adaptive viewport-placement contract without domain branches.

phase2Candidates.name: categorized Settings navigation
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: A second consumer copies the same tab/panel, roving-focus, opener-restore, and responsive-navigation contract without app-specific category logic.

phase2Candidates.name: Settings controls and history coordination
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Both consumers retain native switch ownership and the same header, help-metadata, and callback-driven history coordination without moving app state or reset meaning into the kit.

phase2Candidates.name: portable color-scheme libraries and editor coordination
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Both apps use the same five-role interface palette with an optional complete canvas group, overlay, strict version-3 document, and callback editor contracts while retaining factory values, application, persistence, history, file I/O, and domain redraws locally.

phase2Candidates.name: action controls and segmented presentation
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Both consumers use host-owned icon catalogs and action callbacks behind the same accessible icon binding, activation feedback, and gapless segmented presentation contract.

phase2Candidates.name: compact and expanded tooltip coordination
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Both consumers supply help text and preference state to the same pointer, focus, composite-region, viewport, and dialog-local mounting mechanics.

phase2Candidates.name: UI state normalization
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Both apps persist the same normalized state shape without host-specific branches in the normalizer.

phase2Candidates.name: menu presentation mechanics
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Menu behavior needs only host menu definitions, enabled predicates, and action callbacks.

phase2Candidates.name: results pane state application
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Both apps apply hidden, split, expanded, and responsive states through the same DOM contract.

phase2Candidates.name: typed preference adapter boundary
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Each preference has one explicit read and write owner without a local fallback store.

phase2Candidates.name: engineering library picker and dialog lifecycle
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: A second consumer proves the same record-agnostic adapter without engineering or schema branches.

phase2Candidates.name: visual shell and pane interaction candidates
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Consumers agree on semantic surfaces and interaction contracts while retaining app-owned dimensions and persistence.

phase2Candidates.name: wheel and trackpad gesture classification and frame coordination
phase2Candidates.promotionCriterion: Consumers classify pan versus pinch without platform-only detection, preserve every raw delta in app-owned view state, and coalesce lightweight rendering plus publication to one animation frame.

runtime.remainingReferences: Other contracts remain reference/adapted until consumer evidence proves promotion.

optional3d.boundary: Host callbacks and presentation only; scene, model and geometry remain app-owned.
